strings.lesson.first-words.title: Welcome: first words with {npc:guide}
strings.lesson.first-words.text: A short introduction: hello, yes and no, what is this, and what to say when you are stuck, then the camp.
strings.lesson.first-words.summary: You can greet, say yes and no, ask what something is, and get unstuck: I don't know, again, slower.
strings.lesson.first-words.u1-welcome.text: This is {npc:guide}, the guide. She teaches you Spanish one phrase at a time. Nothing here is a test. Enter goes on, H helps, K skips a step.
strings.lesson.first-words.u1-say-hola.help: Say: Hola (OH-lah). It means hello. The letter h is silent in Spanish.
strings.lesson.first-words.u1-say-hola.retry: Not quite. Say: Hola. It means hello.
strings.lesson.first-words.u1-name.text: {npc:guide} tells you her name. “Me llamo” means “my name is”. You only need to understand this one, not say it.
strings.lesson.first-words.u2-intro.text: Next: yes and no. {npc:guide} holds things up and asks about them. Answer “Sí” for yes or “No” for no.
strings.lesson.first-words.u2-ask-wood.text: {npc:guide} holds up a log of wood and asks if it is wood. “Madera” means wood.
strings.lesson.first-words.u2-yes.text: It is wood, so the answer is yes. Say “Sí” (SEE).
strings.lesson.first-words.u2-yes.help: Say: Sí (SEE). It means yes. It is written sí, with an accent; si without the accent means “if”.
strings.lesson.first-words.u2-yes.retry: Not quite. It is wood, so say: Sí.
strings.lesson.first-words.u2-no.text: She holds up the same log and asks if it is water. It is not: answer “No”.
strings.lesson.first-words.u2-no.retry: Not quite. A log is not water, so say: No.
strings.lesson.first-words.u3-intro.text: Now ask what things are. “¿Qué es esto?” means “What is this?”. {npc:guide} points at something and names it.
strings.lesson.first-words.u3-ask-1.text: {npc:guide} points at a log. Ask her: “¿Qué es esto?” (keh ehs EHS-toh).
strings.lesson.first-words.u3-ask-1.help: Say: ¿Qué es esto? It means what is this?
strings.lesson.first-words.u3-ask-2.text: {npc:guide} points at some fruit. Ask again.
strings.lesson.first-words.u3-is-2.text: “Una fruta” is “a fruit”: una means a. Madera and agua need no una, just like wood and water in English.
strings.lesson.first-words.u3-ask-3.text: {npc:guide} holds up a bottle of water.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4-intro.text: Good manners. When someone offers you something, “Sí, por favor” means “yes, please”, and “Gracias” means “thank you”.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4-offer.text: {npc:guide} offers you some fruit. “¿Quieres…?” means “do you want…?”.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4-yes.text: You would like some. Say: “Sí, por favor” (SEE, por fah-VOR).
strings.lesson.first-class.u4-yes.help: Say: Sí, por favor. It means yes, please.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4-yes.retry: Not quite. Say: Sí, por favor.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4-take.text: {npc:guide} nods at the berry bushes. You pick the fruit yourself.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4-pick.text: Press Esc to close this panel. Aim the dot at a berry bush (the arrow shows one) and hold the left mouse button to pick a fruit. Then walk back to {npc:guide} and press E.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4-pick.help: A berry bush is a green bush with red berries. Hold the left mouse button until the fruit drops into your bar.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4-pick.hud: Pick a fruit from a berry bush, then go back to {npc:guide}
strings.lesson.first-class.u4-thanks.text: You have the fruit. Thank {npc:guide}: say “Gracias” (GRAH-see-ahs).
strings.lesson.first-class.u4-thanks.translation: Very good! You have a fruit.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4-thanks.help: Say: Gracias. It means thank you.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4-thanks.retry: Not quite. Say: Gracias. It means thank you.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4-welcome.text: “De nada” is the polite answer to “gracias”.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4v-intro.text: Spanish verbs change their ending for who does them. For “I” (yo) the ending is -o; for “you” (tú) it is -as or -es: “quiero” is “I want”, “quieres” is “you want”. Some verbs also change in the middle: “tienes” (you have), but “tengo” (I have). {npc:guide} asks about you; answer about yourself, with -o.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4v-ask-want.text: {npc:guide} asks what you want. “Quieres” is “you want”: the ending -es is for you.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4v-say-want.text: You want wood. Say it: “Quiero madera” (kee-EH-roh mah-DEH-rah). “Quiero” is “I want”: the ending -o is for I.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4v-say-want.help: Say: Quiero madera. It means I want wood.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4v-say-want.personRe: Answer about yourself: the ending -o, like “quiero”, “tengo”, “necesito”.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4v-ask-have.text: {npc:guide} asks if you have a fruit: “tienes” is “you have”. You do: say “Tengo una fruta”. Tener changes in the middle: tienes, but tengo.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4v-ask-have.help: Say: Tengo una fruta. It means I have a fruit. Tengo is I have; tienes is you have.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4v-ask-have.retry: Not quite. Say: Tengo una fruta.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4v-ask-have.personRe: Answer about yourself: the ending -o, like “quiero”, “tengo”, “necesito”.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4v-ask-need.text: Now she asks what you need. Answer about yourself, with the -o ending: “Necesito agua”.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4v-ask-need.help: Say: Necesito agua. It means I need water.
strings.lesson.first-class.u4v-ask-need.personRe: Answer about yourself: the ending -o, like “quiero”, “tengo”, “necesito”.
strings.lesson.first-words.u5-intro.text: Everyone gets stuck. Three phrases help: “No sé” (I don't know), “Otra vez, por favor” (again, please) and “Más despacio, por favor” (more slowly, please). The buttons R, S and N do the same.
strings.lesson.first-words.u5-quiz.text: {npc:guide} points at something new. You don't know the word yet, so say “No sé” (noh SEH). It is never wrong.
strings.lesson.first-words.u5-quiz.help: Say: No sé. It means I don't know.
strings.lesson.first-words.u5-quiz.retry: Say: No sé. It means I don't know.
strings.lesson.first-words.u5-answer.text: When you say “No sé”, {npc:guide} tells you the answer.
strings.lesson.first-words.u5-fast.text: {npc:guide} says something longer. Did you catch it?
strings.lesson.first-words.u5-fast.translation: Look. The wood is for the torch.
strings.lesson.first-words.u5-again.text: Ask her to say it again: “Otra vez, por favor” (OH-trah behs, por fah-VOR). She will repeat her last line.
strings.lesson.first-words.u5-again.help: Say: Otra vez, por favor. It means again, please.
strings.lesson.first-words.u5-again.retry: Not quite. Say: Otra vez, por favor.
strings.lesson.first-words.u5-slow.text: Now ask for it more slowly: “Más despacio, por favor” (mahs dehs-PAH-syoh). She will say it slowly.
strings.lesson.first-words.u5-slow.help: Say: Más despacio, por favor. It means more slowly, please.
strings.lesson.first-words.u5-slow.retry: Not quite. Say: Más despacio, por favor.
strings.lesson.first-words.u6-task.text: {npc:guide} explains what the camp needs. What does she say?
strings.lesson.first-words.u6-task.help: “Necesitas” is “you need”. “Madera” is wood and “frutas” is fruit.
strings.lesson.first-words.u6-task.retry: Not quite. Listen again: madera and frutas.
strings.lesson.first-words.u6-task.option.3: You need a torch and a bottle.
strings.lesson.first-words.u6-explain.text: Your list is at the top right. Hold the left mouse button on trees and bushes to collect wood and fruit, make a torch at the workbench (press E) and set it on the fire ring. The village has water.
strings.lesson.first-words.u6-recap.text: You can already say or understand all of this.
strings.lesson.personas.title: Personas: he, she, we, they
strings.lesson.personas.text: Session 2: the verbs for he, she, you (polite), we, you all and they, with the villager and the shopkeeper.
strings.lesson.personas.summary: You can say what she wants and what we need or want, and you know he, she, we and they.
strings.lesson.personas.objective: Session 2: go to the village and talk to the villager to start the lesson “Personas”
strings.lesson.personas.p0-hello.text: The villager greets you. Greet him back, as you learned with {npc:guide}.
strings.lesson.personas.p1-intro.text: Session 2: more people. You know “I” (yo) and “you” (tú). Now: he or she (él, ella), we (nosotros) and they (ellos). The verb ending changes with the person. First a reminder from last time: “Quiero madera” (I want wood). The villager helps first, then you talk to the shopkeeper at the stall. Enter goes on, H helps, K skips a step.
strings.lesson.personas.p1-recall.text: He asks you what you want, with “tú” as {npc:guide} did. Answer about yourself.
strings.lesson.personas.p1-recall.help: Say: Quiero madera. It means I want wood. Quieres is you want; quiero is I want.
strings.lesson.personas.p1-recall.personRetry: Answer about yourself: the ending -o, like “quiero”, “tengo”, “necesito”.
strings.lesson.personas.p1-she-is.text: The villager is talking about {npc:guide}. “Ella” is “she” and “es” is “is”.
strings.lesson.personas.p1-she-is.translation: Luna is the guide. She is my friend.
strings.lesson.personas.p1-ask-luna.text: He asks what {npc:guide} wants. “Quiere” is “he or she wants”. For he or she the ending is -e or -a (quiere, necesita), with no -s.
strings.lesson.personas.p1-say-she.text: Say what she wants: “Ella quiere fruta” (EH-yah kee-EH-reh FROO-tah).
strings.lesson.personas.p1-say-she.help: Say: Ella quiere fruta. It means she wants fruit. Ella is she, so quiere ends in -e.
strings.lesson.personas.p1-say-she.retry: Not quite. Say: Ella quiere fruta.
strings.lesson.personas.p1-say-she.personRetry: Say it about her: the ending -e, like “quiere”, with no -s.
strings.lesson.personas.p2-intro.text: Now “we”: nosotros. The ending is -amos or -emos: necesitamos (we need), queremos (we want), tenemos (we have). No -ie- for we: quiero, but queremos.
strings.lesson.personas.p2-go.text: “Vamos” is “we go” (the verb ir, which does not follow the pattern). Said alone, it means “let's go”. He wants to go to the stall with you.
strings.lesson.personas.p2-ask-we.text: On the way, he asks what the two of you need. Water is on your list. Answer with “we”: “Necesitamos agua”.
strings.lesson.personas.p2-ask-we.help: Say: Necesitamos agua. It means we need water.
strings.lesson.personas.p2-ask-we.personRetry: Say it for the two of you: the ending -amos or -emos, like “necesitamos”, “queremos”.
strings.lesson.personas.p2-they.text: He points at the houses of the village. Now “they”: ellos. The ending is -an or -en: tienen (they have). What does he say?
strings.lesson.personas.p2-they.help: “Ellos” is they, and “tienen” is they have.
strings.lesson.personas.p2-they.retry: Not quite. Listen again: ellos tienen.
strings.lesson.personas.p2-be.text: “Somos” is “we are”: tú y yo (you and I) make nosotros. Somos is from ser, “to be”, which does not follow the pattern.
strings.lesson.personas.p2-where.text: Where is {npc:guide}? “Está” is “is” (estar), as in “¿Dónde está el río?”. Estar is “to be” for where someone is; ser (es, somos) is for what someone is. What does he say?
strings.lesson.personas.p2-where.retry: Not quite. Listen again: ella está.
strings.lesson.personas.p2-walk.text: Press Esc to close this panel. Walk to the stall (the arrow shows it) and press {key:talk} to talk to the shopkeeper.
strings.lesson.personas.p2-walk.help: The stall is the one with the red and white awning in the village.
strings.lesson.personas.p2-walk.hud: Walk to the stall and talk to the shopkeeper
strings.lesson.personas.p3-intro.text: The shopkeeper says “usted”: the polite “you”, for someone you do not know well. Its verb ends like he or she: “necesita”, “tiene”. You still answer about yourself, with the -o of “yo”: “Necesito pan” and “Tengo una botella”. Many shopkeepers say “usted” to customers; he said “tú” last time, and both are normal.
strings.lesson.personas.p3-need.text: He asks what you need. Answer about yourself.
strings.lesson.personas.p3-need.help: Say: Necesito pan. It means I need bread.
strings.lesson.personas.p3-need.personRetry: Answer about yourself: the ending -o, like “quiero”, “tengo”, “necesito”.
strings.lesson.personas.p3-bottle.text: He asks if you have a bottle. Say you do.
strings.lesson.personas.p3-bottle.help: Say: Tengo una botella. It means I have a bottle.
strings.lesson.personas.p3-bottle.retry: Not quite. Say: Tengo una botella.
strings.lesson.personas.p3-bottle.personRetry: Answer about yourself: the ending -o, like “quiero”, “tengo”, “necesito”.
strings.lesson.personas.p4-all.text: Now he speaks to you and the villager together: “ustedes”, “you” for more than one person. In Latin America it is the only plural “you”, for friends and strangers alike. The ending is -en, like ellos: quieren.
strings.lesson.personas.p4-say-we.text: Answer for the two of you: “Queremos pan” (keh-REH-mohs pahn).
strings.lesson.personas.p4-say-we.help: Say: Queremos pan. It means we want bread.
strings.lesson.personas.p4-say-we.personRetry: Say it for the two of you: the ending -amos or -emos, like “necesitamos”, “queremos”.
strings.lesson.personas.p4-they.text: And the people of the village? “Ellos quieren” is “they want”: -en again. What does he say?
strings.lesson.personas.p4-they.retry: Not quite. Listen again: ellos quieren.
strings.lesson.personas.p4-review.text: Before you go, he asks something you have answered before. Answer him.
strings.lesson.personas.p4-table.text: Your new forms. querer: quiere, queremos, quieren. tener: tiene, tenemos, tienen. necesitar: necesita, necesitamos. ser: es, somos. estar: está. ir: vamos. Usted takes the he or she form; ustedes takes the they form. The book keeps them.
strings.lesson.personas.p4-recap.text: You can now say what she wants, what we need and what we want, and you understand he, she, you (polite), we and they.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.title: Ayer y mañana: yesterday and tomorrow
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.text: Session 3: tomorrow with ir a and an infinitive, and a few past forms, with the villager and the shopkeeper.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.summary: You can say what you are going to eat or do tomorrow, and what you ate, drank and where you went yesterday.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.objective: Session 3: go to the village and talk to the villager to start the lesson “Ayer y mañana”
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f0-review.text: First a question from last time. Answer him about yourself or about the two of you.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f0-intro.text: Session 3: yesterday and tomorrow. Three little words: ayer (yesterday), hoy (today) and mañana (tomorrow). First the verb ir, “to go”, and then “ir a” plus a verb, which is how you say what you are going to do. After that, a few past forms at the stall. Enter goes on, H helps, K skips a step.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f1-ir.text: The verb ir, “to go”, does not follow the pattern. I go: voy. You go: vas. He, she, you (polite): va. We go: vamos. They, you all: van. “A” after it is “to”: voy a la tienda is “I go to the shop”. A and el join into al: voy al río.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f1-you-go.text: The villager says what you do today. Which one is it?
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f1-you-go.translati: Today you are going to the shop.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f1-you-go.help: “Vas” is “you go” or “you are going”: the -s is for tú.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f1-you-go.option.1: You are going to the shop today.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f1-you-go.option.2: I am going to the shop today.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f1-you-go.option.3: We are going to the shop today.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-intro.text: Now plans: later today or tomorrow. Like English “going to”: a form of ir, then “a”, then the verb as it is in the dictionary, ending in -ar, -er or -ir (the infinitive). Voy a comer is “I am going to eat”; vamos a comer is “we are going to eat”. A place after “a” is where you go (voy a la tienda); a verb after “a” is what you are going to do. Not “voy a como” (como is “I eat”). “Mañana” can go in front: mañana voy a comer pan.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-ask.text: He asks what you will eat tomorrow. Answer about yourself, with “voy a”: “Voy a comer pan”.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-ask.translation: What are you going to eat tomorrow?
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-ask.help: Say: Voy a comer pan. It means I am going to eat bread.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-ask.retry: Not quite. Say: Voy a comer pan.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-ask.personRetry: Say it about yourself: “voy a”, like “voy”.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-ask.tenseRetry: For a plan, use voy, then “a”, then the infinitive: “voy a comer”.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-ask.presentNote: That is right too. Here we practise “voy a comer”: Voy a comer pan.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-we.text: Now he asks about the two of you. Answer with “vamos a”: “Vamos a comer fruta”. Said as a suggestion, vamos a comer also means “let's eat”.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-we.translation: What are we going to eat?
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-we.help: Say: Vamos a comer fruta. It means we are going to eat fruit.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-we.retry: Not quite. Say: Vamos a comer fruta.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-we.personRetry: Say it for the two of you: “vamos a comer”, like “vamos”.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-we.tenseRetry: For a plan, use vamos, then “a”, then the infinitive: “vamos a comer”.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-we.presentNote: That is right too. Here we practise “vamos a comer”: Vamos a comer fruta.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-they.text: He points at the houses. “Van a comer” is “they are going to eat”. What does he say?
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-they.translation: They are going to eat bread.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-they.help: “Van a comer”: ir, a and an infinitive.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-they.retry: Not quite. Listen again: van a comer.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-they.option.1: They are going to eat bread.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f2-they.option.3: We are going to eat bread.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f3-walk.text: Press Esc to close this panel. Walk to the stall (the arrow shows it) and press {key:talk} to talk to the shopkeeper. He will ask about yesterday.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f3-walk.help: The stall is the one with the red and white awning in the village.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.f3-walk.hud: Walk to the stall and talk to the shopkeeper
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y0-review.text: The shopkeeper asks a question from last time. Answer him.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y0-intro.text: Now yesterday: ayer. Something that is over uses another form, the past. First comer: I ate is comí, you ate is comiste. With “ayer” use the past, not “ayer como” or “ayer voy”.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y1-model.text: He tells you what he ate. “Comí” is “I ate” (comer). In the past, -í is for “I” and -iste is for “you”: comí, comiste.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y1-ate.text: He asks what you ate yesterday. Answer about yourself, in the past: “Ayer comí fruta”.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y1-ate.help: Say: Ayer comí fruta. It means yesterday I ate fruit.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y1-ate.retry: Not quite. Say: Ayer comí fruta.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y1-ate.personRetry: Say it about yourself: the ending -í, like “comí”, not “comiste”.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y1-ate.tenseRetry: Yesterday uses the past form: “comí” (I ate), not “como” or “voy a comer”.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y2-ask.text: He asks if you went to the river. “Fuiste” is “you went”: the past of ir, which does not follow the pattern. For “I” it is “fui”. It still ends in -iste for “you”.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y2-ask.translation: Did you go to the river yesterday?
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y2-went.text: Say that you went: “Ayer fui al río” (ah-YEHR fwee ahl REE-oh).
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y2-went.help: Say: Ayer fui al río. It means yesterday I went to the river.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y2-went.retry: Not quite. Say: Ayer fui al río.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y2-went.tenseRetry: Yesterday uses the past: “fui” (I went), not “voy”.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y4-you.text: Now a form for “you”. What does he say?
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y4-you.translation: Yesterday you went to the river.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y4-you.retry: Not quite. Listen again: ayer fuiste.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y4-you.option.1: Yesterday you went to the river.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y4-you.option.2: Yesterday I went to the river.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y4-you.option.3: Tomorrow you are going to the river.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y3-had.text: He asks if you drank water yesterday. Say you did: “Ayer bebí agua”. Beber is “to drink”, and it works like comer: bebí, bebiste.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y3-had.help: Say: Ayer bebí agua. It means yesterday I drank water.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y3-had.retry: Say the whole sentence, in the past: Ayer bebí agua.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y3-had.tenseRetry: Yesterday uses the past: “bebí” (I drank), not “bebo”.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y5-contrast.text: Yesterday and tomorrow side by side. “Ayer fui al río” has a past form, “I went”. “Mañana voy a ir al río” has voy a and the infinitive, “I am going to go”. The usual slip is to mix them: “mañana fui” or “ayer voy”. The game will tell you.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y6-tomorrow.text: Last question: tomorrow. Say you are going to go to the river. Not “fui”: that was yesterday.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y6-tomorrow.transla: What are you going to do tomorrow?
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y6-tomorrow.help: Say: Mañana voy a ir al río. It means tomorrow I am going to go to the river.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y6-tomorrow.retry: Not quite. Say: Mañana voy a ir al río.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y6-tomorrow.personR: Say it about yourself: “voy a”, like “voy”.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y6-tomorrow.tenseRe: Tomorrow uses “voy a” and the infinitive: “voy a ir”, not “fui”.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y6-tomorrow.present: That is right too. Here we practise “voy a ir”: Mañana voy a ir al río.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y7-table.text: Your new forms. ir: voy, vas, va, vamos, van. Plans: voy a comer, vamos a comer, van a comer, voy a ir. Yesterday: comí, comiste; bebí, bebiste; fui, fuiste. Fui is also the past of ser (“I was”); here it means “I went”. The book keeps them.
strings.lesson.ayer-y-manana.y8-recap.text: You can now say what you are going to eat or do tomorrow, and what you ate, drank and where you went yesterday. Hoy is today.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.title: El pueblo: the village
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.text: Session 4: places and the way to them, with {npc:fisher} the fisher at the bridge and the villager: ¿Dónde está…?, cerca and lejos, hay, and your own walk told now, as a plan and once it is over.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.summary: You can ask where a place is and if it is far, ask if there is something, and say where you are going, what you are going to do there and where you went.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.objective: Session 4: walk down the road to the bridge and talk to {npc:fisher}, the fisher, to start the lesson “El pueblo”
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v0-hello.text: {npc:fisher} the fisher greets you. Greet him back, as you learned with {npc:guide}.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v0-intro.text: Session 4: the village. {npc:fisher} fishes by the bridge and knows every place. You ask him the way, walk there, and come back to tell him where you went. Enter goes on, H helps, K skips a step.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v1-bakery.text: He asks what you are looking for. Ask where the bakery is: “¿Dónde está la panadería?” ¿Dónde está…? works for any place, with el or la: la panadería ends in -a.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v1-bakery.help: Say: ¿Dónde está la panadería? It means where is the bakery?
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v1-bakery.retry: Not quite. Say: ¿Dónde está la panadería?
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v1-left.text: Izquierda is left and derecha is right. Which does he say?
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v1-left.translation: In the village, look at the tower. The bakery is on the left.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v1-left.help: “A la izquierda” is “on the left”; “a la derecha” is “on the right”.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v1-left.retry: Not quite. Listen again: a la izquierda.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v1-left.option.1: The bakery is left of the tower.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v1-left.option.2: The bakery is right of the tower.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v1-left.option.3: The bakery is next to the river.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v1-smithy.text: He asks if you want anything else. Ask for the smithy the same way: “¿Dónde está la herrería?”
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v1-smithy.help: Say: ¿Dónde está la herrería? It means where is the smithy?
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v1-smithy.retry: Not quite. Say: ¿Dónde está la herrería?
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v1-right.text: The smithy is on the other side of the tower: a la derecha, on the right.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v1-right.translation: And the smithy is on the right.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v2-far.text: Ask if it is far: “¿Está lejos?” Lejos is far and cerca is near. Where things are takes estar: está lejos, not “es lejos”.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v2-far.help: Say: ¿Está lejos? It means is it far?
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v2-near.translation: No, it is near. The mountain is far.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v2-near.retry: Not quite. Listen again: está cerca.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v2-near.option.1: No, it is near. The mountain is far.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v2-near.option.2: Yes, it is far. The mountain is near.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v2-near.option.3: No, it is far. The mountain is near.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v3-houses.text: Hay is “there is” or “there are”. What is in the village?
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v3-houses.translation: In the village there is a shop, a bakery and three houses.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v3-houses.help: “Hay” is there is or there are; “tres casas” is three houses.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v3-houses.retry: Not quite. Listen again: tres casas.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v3-houses.option.1: A shop, a bakery and three houses.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v3-houses.option.2: A shop, a bakery and two houses.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v3-houses.option.3: A bakery, a smithy and a well.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v3-well.text: He did not name a well. Ask if there is one: “¿Hay un pozo en el pueblo?” Pozo is masculine: un pozo.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v3-well.help: Say: ¿Hay un pozo en el pueblo? It means is there a well in the village?
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v3-well.retry: Not quite. Say: ¿Hay un pozo en el pueblo?
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v4-going.text: Now your walk, in three times. Voy a and a place is where you are going now: voy a la panadería. He asks where you are going: “Voy a la panadería”.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v4-going.help: Say: Voy a la panadería. It means I am going to the bakery.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v4-going.retry: Not quite. Say: Voy a la panadería.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v4-going.tenseRetry: You are going now: “voy” (I go), not “fui”.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v4-plan.text: Voy a and a verb is a plan, as in session 3 (voy a comer). He asks what you are going to do there. Comprar is to buy: “Voy a comprar pan”.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v4-plan.translation: What are you going to do there?
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v4-plan.help: Say: Voy a comprar pan. It means I am going to buy bread.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v4-plan.retry: Not quite. Say: Voy a comprar pan.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v4-plan.personRetry: Say it about yourself: “voy a comprar”.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v4-plan.tenseRetry: For a plan, use voy, then “a”, then the infinitive: “voy a comprar”, not “compro”.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v4-plan.presentNote: That is right too. Here we practise “voy a comprar”: Voy a comprar pan.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v5-bakery.text: Press Esc to close this panel and follow the arrow to the bakery (la panadería), left of the tower.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v5-bakery.help: Follow the road into the village; the bakery is the timber house with the oven by its wall.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v5-smithy.text: Now the smithy (la herrería), on the other side of the tower. Follow the arrow.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v5-smithy.help: The smithy is the house with the fire outside its door, right of the tower.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v5-villager.text: Now go to the villager in the square and press {key:talk} to talk to him.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v5-villager.help: The villager stands in the square, south of the tower.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v5-villager.hud: Talk to the villager in the square
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v6-sign.text: He reads the signpost. “Dice” is “it says”. What does it say?
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v6-sign.translation: The sign says: shop, river, mountain.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v6-sign.help: “El letrero” is the sign and “dice” is says.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v6-sign.retry: Not quite. Listen again: tienda, río, montaña.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v6-sign.option.1: The sign says: shop, river, mountain.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v6-sign.option.2: The sign says: bakery, smithy, well.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v6-sign.option.3: The shop is next to the river.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v6-back.text: Press Esc and go back to {npc:fisher} at the bridge (the arrow shows it). Press {key:talk} to talk to him.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v6-back.help: Follow the road out of the village, west, to the bridge.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v6-back.hud: Go back to {npc:fisher} at the bridge
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v7-went.text: He asks if you went to the bakery. You did, and it is over: say “Sí” and the past, “Sí, fui a la panadería” (fui: I went, as in session 3).
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v7-went.translation: Did you go to the bakery?
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v7-went.help: Say: Sí, fui a la panadería. It means yes, I went to the bakery.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v7-went.retry: Not quite. Say: Sí, fui a la panadería.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v7-went.tenseRetry: That walk is over: use the past, “fui” (I went), not “voy”.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v7-hungry.text: {npc:fisher} is hungry. Bring him three fruits from the bushes at {npc:guide}'s camp and hand them over in Spanish, “Aquí tienes tres frutas”: he pays you two coins. It can wait; the objective line keeps it.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v7-hungry.translation: I am hungry. Do you have any fruit?
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v8-thanks.text: He says you know the village now. Thank him.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v8-table.text: One verb in three times, around your walk. Now: voy a la panadería (I am going to the bakery). The plan: voy a comprar pan (I am going to buy bread). Over: fui a la panadería (I went to the bakery). For places: ¿Dónde está…?, está cerca or lejos (estar, not ser), a la izquierda, a la derecha, and hay (there is, there are). The book keeps them.
strings.lesson.el-pueblo.v8-recap.text: You can now ask where a place is and if it is far, ask if there is something, and say where you are going, what you are going to do there and where you went. Next session: {npc:baker}, the baker, waits for you at the bakery.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.title: Números y pan: numbers and bread
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.text: Session 5: numbers, plurals and prices with {npc:baker} the baker: ¿Cuántos…?, ¿Cuánto cuesta?, and her order told as a plan, in the present and once it is done, with the past of -ar verbs (compré).
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.summary: You can count to ten, ask how many and how much, ask for a number of things, and say what you are going to do, what you have and what you bought.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.objective: Session 5: go to the bakery (la panadería), left of the tower, and talk to {npc:baker}, the baker, to start the lesson “Números y pan”
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n0-review.text: {npc:baker} the baker greets you and asks something you have answered before. Answer her.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n0-intro.text: Session 5: numbers and bread. {npc:baker} bakes the village's bread. She counts her loaves, sells them for coins, and needs wood for her oven. Enter goes on, H helps, K skips a step.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n1-five.text: Uno, dos, tres… She counts her loaves. Which numbers does she say?
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n1-five.help: Uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco: one to five.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n1-five.retry: Not quite. Listen again: uno, dos, tres.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n1-ten.text: She counts on. Which numbers now?
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n1-ten.help: Seis, siete, ocho, nueve, diez: six to ten.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n1-ten.retry: Not quite. Listen again: seis, siete, ocho.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n1-loaves.text: She has ten loaves. One loaf is un pan; more are panes. A word that ends in a consonant adds -es, one that ends in a vowel adds -s: una moneda, dos monedas.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n2-want.text: She asks how many loaves you want. Ask for two: “Quiero dos panes”, and por favor. The number comes before the noun, and the noun is plural.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n2-want.translation: How many loaves do you want?
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n2-want.help: Say: Quiero dos panes, por favor. It means I want two loaves, please.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n2-want.retry: Not quite. Say: Quiero dos panes, por favor.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n2-price.text: Bread costs coins. Ask the price: “¿Cuánto cuesta?” Cuánto is how much, and cuesta is it costs.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n2-price.help: Say: ¿Cuánto cuesta? It means how much is it?
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n2-two.help: “Cuesta” is costs and “dos monedas” is two coins.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n2-two.retry: Not quite. Listen again: dos monedas.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n3-oven.text: Her oven needs wood, and she will pay four coins for five blocks. She asks what you are going to do. A plan is voy a and an infinitive, as in session 4: “Voy a buscar madera” (buscar: to look for).
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n3-oven.translation: I need five blocks of wood for the oven. I will pay you four coins. What are you going to do?
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n3-oven.help: Say: Voy a buscar madera. It means I am going to look for wood.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n3-oven.retry: Not quite. Say: Voy a buscar madera.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n3-oven.personRetry: Say it about yourself: “voy a buscar”.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n3-oven.tenseRetry: For a plan, use voy, then “a”, then the infinitive: “voy a buscar”, not “busco”.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n3-oven.presentNote: That is right too. Here we practise “voy a buscar”: Voy a buscar madera.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n4-wood.text: Press Esc to close this panel and follow the arrow to the trees at the forest's edge. Aim the dot at a trunk and hold the left mouse button to collect wood (madera).
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n4-wood.help: The trees stand round the village's clearing; the arrow shows the nearest one.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n4-wood.hud: Collect wood (madera) at the forest's edge
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n4-back.text: Collect five wood in all, then take it to {npc:baker} at the bakery and press {key:talk}. She asks what you have: hand it over in Spanish, “Aquí tienes cinco bloques de madera” (here are five blocks of wood), or just “Aquí tienes la madera”.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n4-back.help: Five pieces of wood (madera): your bar shows how many you have. The bakery is the timber house with the oven, left of the tower.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n4-back.hud: Take five wood (madera) to {npc:baker} at the bakery
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n5-coins.text: She takes the wood and pays you. How many coins?
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n5-coins.translatio: Thank you! Here are four coins.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n5-coins.retry: Not quite. Listen again: cuatro monedas.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n5-have.text: Now the present: she asks how many coins you have (cuántas, because monedas is feminine). Count them: “Tengo cuatro monedas”.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n5-have.translation: How many coins do you have?
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n5-have.help: Say: Tengo cuatro monedas. It means I have four coins.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n5-have.retry: Not quite. Say: Tengo cuatro monedas.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n5-have.tenseRetry: You have them now: use the present, “tengo” (I have).
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n6-buy.text: Now you can pay. Buy two loaves: say “Quiero dos panes, por favor”. Two loaves cost four coins.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n6-buy.help: Say: Quiero dos panes, por favor. A loaf costs two coins.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n7-model.text: Comprar in the past: compré, I bought (the stress on the -é). An -ar verb ends in -é for yo, as comí and bebí end in -í. She tells you what she bought yesterday.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n7-model.translatio: Yesterday I bought fruit at the shop.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n7-bought.text: She asks what you bought. The purchase is over: say it in the past, “Compré dos panes”.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n7-bought.help: Say: Compré dos panes. It means I bought two loaves.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n7-bought.retry: Not quite. Say: Compré dos panes.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n7-bought.tenseRetr: The purchase is over: use the past, “compré” (I bought), not “compro”.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n7-you.text: Compraste is the tú form, you bought (-aste). What does she say?
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n7-you.translation: You bought two loaves. Very good!
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n7-you.help: “Compraste” is you bought; “compré” is I bought.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n7-you.option.3: You are going to buy two loaves.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n8-walk.text: The stall sells her bread too. Press Esc, follow the arrow to the stall (la tienda) and press {key:talk} to talk to the shopkeeper.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n8-walk.help: The stall is a few steps from the bakery, towards the square.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n8-walk.hud: Talk to the shopkeeper at the stall
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n8-hay.text: Ask him if there is bread: “¿Hay pan?” Hay is there is, as in session 4.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n8-hay.help: Say: ¿Hay pan? It means is there any bread?
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n8-luz.translation: Yes, there is bread. It is Luz's bread.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n8-no.text: He offers you bread. You have two loaves already: say no.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n9-table.text: Numbers: uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco, seis, siete, ocho, nueve, diez. More than one: pan, panes; moneda, monedas. How many: ¿cuántos panes?, ¿cuántas monedas? How much: ¿cuánto cuesta? (cuesta for one thing, cuestan for more). Around her order: the plan, voy a buscar madera; now, tengo cuatro monedas; over, compré dos panes (compré: I bought; compraste: you bought). The book keeps them.
strings.lesson.numeros-y-pan.n9-recap.text: You can now count to ten, ask how many and how much, ask for a number of things, and say what you are going to do, what you have and what you bought. Next session: the villager in the square shows you {npc:smith}, the smith, at the smithy.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.title: Gente del pueblo: the people of the village
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.text: Session 6: who is who in the village, with the villager, {npc:smith} the smith and {npc:farmer} the farmer: ¿Cómo te llamas?, ¿Qué haces?, vivo en, trabaja en, and the axe {npc:smith} makes for you, told before, now and once it is made: about someone else for the first time.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.summary: You can ask someone's name and what they do, say where you live, and say who someone is, where he works, what he is going to make and what he made.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.objective: Session 6: go to the square and talk to the villager, who will show you {npc:smith} the smith, to start the lesson “Gente del pueblo”
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g0-review.text: The villager greets you and asks something you have answered before. Answer him.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g0-intro.text: Session 6: the people of the village. You meet {npc:smith} the smith and {npc:farmer} the farmer, ask their names and what they do, and tell the villager about {npc:smith}: what he is going to make, where he works and what he made. Enter goes on, H helps, K skips a step.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g1-smith.text: The villager shows you a man by the smithy, across the square. Está says where he is; es says who he is.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g1-smith.transla: Look, there is Domingo. He is the smith.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g1-who.text: He asks who Domingo is. Answer with es and the job: “Es el herrero”.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g1-who.help: Say: Es el herrero. It means he is the smith.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g1-who.retry: Not quite. Say: Es el herrero.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g1-axe.text: Domingo wants to make something for you: quiere hacer is he wants to make, and te is for you.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g1-axe.translati: Domingo wants to make an axe for you.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g1-plan.text: Say his plan for him: va a and an infinitive, as you say voy a for yourself. “Va a hacer un hacha”. Hacha is feminine, but it takes un and el because it starts with a stressed a.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g1-plan.translat: What is Domingo going to make?
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g1-plan.help: Say: Va a hacer un hacha. It means he is going to make an axe.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g1-plan.retry: Not quite. Say: Va a hacer un hacha.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g1-plan.personRe: Say it about him: “va a hacer”, not “voy a hacer”.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g1-plan.tenseRet: It is his plan: use va, then “a”, then the infinitive: “va a hacer”, not “hace”.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g1-plan.presentN: That is right too. Here we practise “va a hacer”: Va a hacer un hacha.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g2-walk.text: Press Esc, follow the arrow to {npc:smith} by the smithy and press {key:talk} to talk to him.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g2-walk.help: The smithy is the house right of the tower, with the forge by its door.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g2-walk.hud: Talk to {npc:smith} the smith at the smithy
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g3-name.text: He greets you. Ask his name: “¿Cómo te llamas?”
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g3-name.help: Say: ¿Cómo te llamas? It means what is your name?
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g3-name.personRe: He says tú to you: ask with tú, “¿Cómo te llamas?”
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g3-llamo.text: He tells you his name: me llamo, I am called.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g3-job.text: Now ask what he does: “¿Qué haces?” Hacer is to do or to make.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g3-job.help: Say: ¿Qué haces? It means what do you do?
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g3-smith.transla: I am the smith. I work with fire and wood.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g3-smith.help: “Herrero” is smith and “trabajo” is I work.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g3-smith.retry: Not quite. Listen again: soy el herrero.
He is the smith: fire and wood.
He is the farmer: the field.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g3-lives.text: He asks where you live. Answer with vivo, I live: “Vivo en el campamento”.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g3-lives.help: Say: Vivo en el campamento. It means I live at the camp.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g3-lives.retry: Not quite. Say: Vivo en el campamento.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g3-lives.tenseRe: Where you live now: use the present, “vivo” (I live).
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g4-offer.text: He offers to make the axe. What does he need for it?
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g4-offer.transla: Do you want an axe? I need two blocks of wood and two coins.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g4-offer.help: “Dos bloques de madera y dos monedas” is two blocks of wood and two coins.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g4-offer.retry: Not quite. Listen again: dos bloques de madera y dos monedas.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g4-wood.text: Press Esc to close this panel and follow the arrow to the trees at the forest's edge. Aim the dot at a trunk and hold the left mouse button to collect wood (madera).
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g4-wood.help: The trees stand round the village's clearing; the arrow shows the nearest one.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g4-wood.hud: Collect wood (madera) at the forest's edge
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g4-back.text: Collect two wood in all, then take it to {npc:smith} at the smithy with two coins and press {key:talk}. He asks what you have: hand them over in Spanish, “Aquí tienes la madera y las monedas” (here are the wood and the coins).
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g4-back.help: Two pieces of wood (madera) and two coins: your bar shows how many you have. No coins? {npc:fisher} at the bridge pays two for three fruits.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g4-back.hud: Take two wood (madera) and two coins to {npc:smith} at the smithy
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g4-axe.text: He takes the wood and the coins and gives you the axe. With it in your hand, a trunk falls four times faster.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g4-axe.translati: Thank you! Here is the axe.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g5-walk.text: Now meet the farmer. Press Esc, follow the arrow to {npc:farmer} at the wheat field and press {key:talk}.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g5-walk.help: The field is east of the square, between two houses.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g5-walk.hud: Talk to the farmer at the field
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g5-name.text: He greets you. Ask his name too: “¿Cómo te llamas?”
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g5-name.help: Say: ¿Cómo te llamas? It means what is your name?
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g5-name.personRe: He says tú to you: ask with tú, “¿Cómo te llamas?”
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g5-job.text: He tells you what he does.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g5-job.translati: I am the farmer. I work in the field.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g6-walk.text: Go back to the villager in the square and press {key:talk}: he wants to know about {npc:smith}.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g6-walk.help: The villager stands in the square, a few steps west of the field.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g6-walk.hud: Talk to the villager in the square
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g6-works.text: He asks where Domingo works. Domingo said trabajo, I work; for him it is trabaja: “Domingo trabaja en la herrería”.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g6-works.help: Say: Domingo trabaja en la herrería. It means Domingo works at the smithy.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g6-works.retry: Not quite. Say: Domingo trabaja en la herrería.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g6-works.tenseRe: He works there now: use the present, “trabaja”.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g6-house.text: He tells you where Domingo lives. What does he say?
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g6-house.transla: Domingo lives in a house near the smithy.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g6-house.help: “Vive” is he lives and “cerca de” is near.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g6-house.retry: Not quite. Listen again: vive en una casa.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g6-made.text: The axe is made. He asks what Domingo made: say it in the past, hizo (he made): “Domingo hizo un hacha”.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g6-made.help: Say: Domingo hizo un hacha. It means Domingo made an axe.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g6-made.retry: Not quite. Say: Domingo hizo un hacha.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g6-made.tenseRet: It is done: use the past, “hizo” (he made), not “hace”.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g6-much.text: Trabajó, he worked: the -ar past for él and ella, stressed on the -ó. What does he say?
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g6-much.help: “Ayer” is yesterday and “trabajó” is he worked.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g6-much.retry: Not quite. Listen again: ayer, trabajó.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g6-much.option.3: Tomorrow he will work a lot.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g7-review.text: He asks something you have answered before. Answer him.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g7-table.text: Names: ¿Cómo te llamas? Me llamo Domingo. Jobs: ¿Qué haces? Soy el herrero; es el herrero (who someone is: ser). Places: vivo en, trabaja en (vivir: vivo, vives, vive; trabajar: trabajo, trabaja). About someone else, in three times: now, Domingo trabaja en la herrería; the plan, va a hacer un hacha; over, hizo un hacha (hacer: hace, va a hacer, hizo), and trabajó, he worked. Un hacha, el hacha: hacha is feminine. The book keeps them.
strings.lesson.gente-del-pueblo.g7-recap.text: You can now ask someone's name and what they do, say where you live, and say who someone is, where he works, what he is going to make and what he made. Next time, {npc:farmer} has apples and an errand for you at the field.
strings.lesson.como-es.title: ¿Cómo es?: what things are like
strings.lesson.como-es.text: Session 7: what things are like and what you like, with {npc:farmer} the farmer and the shopkeeper: la manzana es roja (the adjective after the noun, agreeing with it), me gusta and me gustan, me gustó in the past, and the water {npc:farmer} needs for his plants, told before you fetch it and after.
strings.lesson.como-es.summary: You can say what something is like (la manzana es roja, es grande), ask for things with an adjective (tres manzanas rojas), and say what you like (me gusta, me gustan) and what you liked (me gustó).
strings.lesson.como-es.objective: Session 7: go to the field and talk to {npc:farmer} the farmer to start the lesson “¿Cómo es?”
strings.lesson.como-es.c0-review.text: {npc:farmer} greets you and asks something you have answered before. Answer him.
strings.lesson.como-es.c0-intro.text: Session 7: what things are like. An adjective says it: roja (red), grande (big). In Spanish it comes after the noun and agrees with it: la manzana roja, las manzanas rojas. You also say what you like, me gusta, and what you liked, me gustó. Enter goes on, H helps, K skips a step.
strings.lesson.como-es.c1-apples.text: {npc:farmer} shows you his apples. What are they like?
strings.lesson.como-es.c1-apples.translation: Look at my apples. They are red and big.
strings.lesson.como-es.c1-apples.help: “Rojas” is red and “grandes” is big. Rojas ends in -as because manzanas is feminine and plural; grande only takes an -s.
strings.lesson.como-es.c1-apples.retry: Not quite. Listen again: rojas y grandes.
strings.lesson.como-es.c1-how.text: He asks what the apple is like. Say es (it is) and the adjective, which agrees with la manzana: “La manzana es roja”, not rojo.
strings.lesson.como-es.c1-how.help: Say: La manzana es roja. It means the apple is red.
strings.lesson.como-es.c1-how.retry: Not quite. Say: La manzana es roja.
strings.lesson.como-es.c1-how.personRetry: Say it about the apple: “es”, it is.
strings.lesson.como-es.c2-bread.text: He asks if you like bread. Say “Sí” and gustar, which says it the other way round: me gusta el pan, bread pleases me. “Sí, me gusta el pan”.
strings.lesson.como-es.c2-bread.help: Say: Sí, me gusta el pan. It means yes, I like bread.
strings.lesson.como-es.c2-bread.retry: Not quite. Say: Sí, me gusta el pan.
strings.lesson.como-es.c2-bread.personRetry: One thing pleases you, el pan: “me gusta”, not “me gustan”.
strings.lesson.como-es.c2-bread.tenseRetry: You like it now: “me gusta”, not “me gustó”.
strings.lesson.como-es.c2-apples.text: Now the apples. “Sí” again, and gustar takes -n, because more than one thing pleases you: “Sí, me gustan las manzanas”.
strings.lesson.como-es.c2-apples.help: Say: Sí, me gustan las manzanas. It means yes, I like apples.
strings.lesson.como-es.c2-apples.retry: Not quite. Say: Sí, me gustan las manzanas.
strings.lesson.como-es.c2-apples.personRetry: Las manzanas are more than one: “me gustan”, with -n.
strings.lesson.como-es.c3-want.text: He asks how many apples you want. Ask for three red ones: the number before the noun, the adjective after it, “Quiero tres manzanas rojas”. An apple costs one coin.
strings.lesson.como-es.c3-want.translation: How many apples do you want?
strings.lesson.como-es.c3-want.help: Say: Quiero tres manzanas rojas. It means I want three red apples.
strings.lesson.como-es.c3-want.retry: Not quite. Say: Quiero tres manzanas rojas.
strings.lesson.como-es.c3-plan.text: His plants need water, and he gives apples for it. Say your plan with voy a and an infinitive, as for {npc:baker}'s wood: “Voy a buscar agua”.
strings.lesson.como-es.c3-plan.translation: My plants need water. If you bring me water from the river, I will give you three apples. What are you going to do?
strings.lesson.como-es.c3-plan.help: Say: Voy a buscar agua. It means I am going to fetch water.
strings.lesson.como-es.c3-plan.retry: Not quite. Say: Voy a buscar agua.
strings.lesson.como-es.c3-plan.personRetry: Say it about yourself: “voy a buscar”.
strings.lesson.como-es.c3-plan.tenseRetry: It is your plan: use voy, then “a”, then the infinitive: “voy a buscar”, not “busco”.
strings.lesson.como-es.c3-plan.presentNote: That is right too. Here we practise “voy a buscar”: Voy a buscar agua.
strings.lesson.como-es.c4-walk.text: Press Esc, follow the arrow to the stall on your way to the river and press {key:talk} to talk to the shopkeeper.
strings.lesson.como-es.c4-walk.help: The stall is on the west side of the square, by the road to the bridge.
strings.lesson.como-es.c4-walk.hud: Talk to the shopkeeper at the stall, on your way to the river
strings.lesson.como-es.c4-big.text: He shows you a loaf. What is it like? Grande is the same for el and la: “Es grande”.
strings.lesson.como-es.c4-big.translation: Look at this bread. What is it like?
strings.lesson.como-es.c4-big.help: Say: Es grande. It means it is big.
strings.lesson.como-es.c4-big.personRetry: Say it about the bread: “es”, it is.
strings.lesson.como-es.c4-luz.text: Whose bread is it? De says whose: el pan de Luz, Luz's bread.
strings.lesson.como-es.c4-luz.translation: The bread is Luz's, from the bakery.
strings.lesson.como-es.c5-river.text: Press Esc and follow the arrow to the river (río) by the bridge, where {npc:fisher} fishes. Fill your bottle there: aim the dot at the water and hold the left mouse button.
strings.lesson.como-es.c5-river.help: The river runs under the bridge, west of the village; {npc:fisher} stands on its bank. No bottle? The shopkeeper gives you one: say “Quiero agua, por favor”.
strings.lesson.como-es.c5-river.hud: Go to the river (río) by the bridge and fill your bottle with water (agua)
strings.lesson.como-es.c5-back.text: Take the water to {npc:farmer} at the field and press {key:talk}. He asks what you have: hand it over in Spanish, “Aquí tienes el agua” (here is the water).
strings.lesson.como-es.c5-back.help: Your bar shows a bottle of water (agua). The field is east of the square.
strings.lesson.como-es.c5-back.hud: Take the water (agua) to {npc:farmer} at the field
strings.lesson.como-es.c5-thanks.text: He takes the water and gives you three apples.
strings.lesson.como-es.c5-thanks.translation: Thank you! Here are three apples.
strings.lesson.como-es.c5-went.text: He asks if you went to the river. Say “Sí” and the past, fui (I went), as in session 3: “Sí, fui al río”.
strings.lesson.como-es.c5-went.translation: Did you go to the river?
strings.lesson.como-es.c5-went.help: Say: Sí, fui al río. It means yes, I went to the river.
strings.lesson.como-es.c5-went.retry: Not quite. Say: Sí, fui al río.
strings.lesson.como-es.c5-went.tenseRetry: You have been there: use the past, “fui”, not “voy”.
strings.lesson.como-es.c6-model.text: Gustar in the past: me gustó, it pleased me, with the stress on the -ó. Listen to {npc:farmer}.
strings.lesson.como-es.c6-model.translation: Yesterday I ate Luz's bread. I liked it a lot!
strings.lesson.como-es.c6-liked.text: He asks if you liked Luz's bread, the bread you bought in session 5. Say “Sí” and the past: “Sí, me gustó el pan de Luz”.
strings.lesson.como-es.c6-liked.help: Say: Sí, me gustó el pan de Luz. It means yes, I liked Luz's bread.
strings.lesson.como-es.c6-liked.retry: Not quite. Say: Sí, me gustó el pan de Luz.
strings.lesson.como-es.c6-liked.personRetry: One thing pleased you, el pan: “me gustó”.
strings.lesson.como-es.c6-liked.tenseRetry: You ate it before: use the past, “me gustó”, not “me gusta”.
strings.lesson.como-es.c7-review.text: He says something to you. Answer him.
strings.lesson.como-es.c7-table.text: What things are like: es and the adjective, which agrees with its noun: la manzana es roja, el pan es grande, las manzanas son rojas. After a noun: tres manzanas rojas. Grande is the same for el and la. What you like: me gusta for one thing (el pan), me gustan for more (las manzanas); in the past, me gustó. The book keeps them.
strings.lesson.como-es.c7-recap.text: You can now say what something is like, ask for things with an adjective, and say what you like and what you liked. Next time, the villager in the square tells you what everyone in the village did yesterday.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.title: Ayer en el pueblo: yesterday in the village
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.text: Session 8: what everyone in the village did yesterday, told by the villager and retold by you to {npc:smith} and {npc:fisher}: the past for él and ella (hizo, pescó, compró), for nosotros (fuimos) and for ellos (comieron), and tengo que, what you have to do now.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.summary: You can say what someone else did (Luz hizo pan, Mar pescó en el río, Luz compró pescado), what you and someone did (fuimos al río), what they did (ellos comieron pan), and what you have to do (tengo que ir al río).
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.objective: Session 8: go to the square and talk to the villager to start the lesson “Ayer en el pueblo”
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a0-review.text: The villager greets you and asks something you have answered before. Answer him.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a0-intro.text: Session 8: yesterday in the village. The villager tells you what everyone did yesterday, and you tell it again, to him, to {npc:smith} and to {npc:fisher}. The past has a form for every person: hizo and pescó for él and ella, fuimos for nosotros, comieron for ellos. You also say what you have to do: tengo que and an infinitive. Enter goes on, H helps, K skips a step.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a1-day.translat: Yesterday Luz made bread. Domingo worked at the smithy. Mar fished in the river.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a1-day.help: “Hizo” is made, “trabajó” is worked and “pescó” is fished: the past for él and ella. The -ó is stressed.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a1-day.retry: Not quite. Listen again: hizo pan, trabajó, pescó.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a1-luz.text: He asks what Luz did yesterday. Say it about her, in the past: hizo (she made), as you said of {npc:smith} in session 6: “Luz hizo pan”.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a1-luz.help: Say: Luz hizo pan. It means Luz made bread.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a1-luz.retry: Not quite. Say: Luz hizo pan.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a1-luz.tenseRet: It was yesterday: use the past, “hizo”, not “hace”.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a1-mar.text: Now Mar. Pescar is to fish; for him, in the past, it ends in a stressed -ó, like trabajó: “Mar pescó en el río”.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a1-mar.help: Say: Mar pescó en el río. It means Mar fished in the river.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a1-mar.retry: Not quite. Say: Mar pescó en el río.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a1-mar.tenseRet: It was yesterday: use the past, “pescó”, not “pesca”.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a2-ate.text: For two people or more, the past of comer ends in -ieron: comieron, they ate. Listen to the villager.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a2-ate.translat: In the afternoon, Luz and Mar ate bread in the square.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a2-we.text: For you and someone else, nosotros, the past of ir is fuimos: we went. Listen to the villager.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a2-we.translati: In the morning, Luz and I went to the shop.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a2-went.text: Yesterday you went to the river for {npc:farmer}'s water, and Mar was there, fishing: you and Mar both went to the river. He asks where you went (fueron, you all went). Answer for the two of you: “Fuimos al río”.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a2-went.transla: And Mar and you? Where did you go yesterday?
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a2-went.help: Say: Fuimos al río. It means we went to the river.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a2-went.retry: Not quite. Say: Fuimos al río.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a2-went.personR: Say it for you and Mar: “fuimos”, we went, not “fui”.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a2-went.tenseRe: It was yesterday: use the past, “fuimos”, not “vamos”.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a2-smith.text: Domingo is looking for you: te busca. Está says where he is.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a2-smith.transl: Domingo is looking for you. He is at the smithy.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a3-walk.text: Press Esc, follow the arrow to {npc:smith} by the smithy and press {key:talk} to talk to him.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a3-walk.help: The smithy is the house right of the tower, with the forge by its door.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a3-walk.hud: Talk to {npc:smith} the smith at the smithy
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a3-ate.text: {npc:smith} worked all day yesterday and asks what Luz and Mar ate. Tell him what the villager told you, with ellos and the past for ellos: “Ellos comieron pan”.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a3-ate.translat: Hello! Yesterday I worked all day. What did Luz and Mar eat?
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a3-ate.help: Say: Ellos comieron pan. It means they ate bread.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a3-ate.retry: Not quite. Say: Ellos comieron pan.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a3-ate.tenseRet: It was yesterday: use the past, “comieron”, not “comen”.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a3-must.text: Mar is looking for you at the river. Tener que and an infinitive says what someone has to do: tienes que ir, you have to go. Say it for yourself, now: “Tengo que ir al río”.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a3-must.transla: Mar went to the river and is looking for you. Where do you have to go?
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a3-must.help: Say: Tengo que ir al río. It means I have to go to the river.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a3-must.retry: Not quite. Say: Tengo que ir al río.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a3-must.personR: Say it about yourself: “tengo que”, not “tienes que”.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a3-must.tenseRe: You have to go now: use the present, “tengo que ir”.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a4-walk.text: So go: press Esc, follow the arrow to the river (río) by the bridge, where {npc:fisher} fishes, and press {key:talk} to talk to him.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a4-walk.help: The river runs under the bridge, west of the village; {npc:fisher} stands on its bank.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a4-walk.hud: Go to {npc:fisher} at the river (río) by the bridge
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a4-sold.transla: Hello! Yesterday I sold fish to Luz. Tomorrow she is going to buy more.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a4-sold.help: “Vendí” is I sold and “va a comprar” is she is going to buy.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a4-sold.retry: Not quite. Listen again: vendí, va a comprar.
He sold her fish; she will buy more.
He will sell her fish tomorrow.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a4-bought.text: He asks what Luz bought. Comprar in the past for her ends in a stressed -ó, like pescó: “Luz compró pescado”.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a4-bought.help: Say: Luz compró pescado. It means Luz bought fish.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a4-bought.retry: Not quite. Say: Luz compró pescado.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a4-bought.tense: It was yesterday: use the past, “compró”, not “compra”.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a5-review.text: {npc:fisher} asks something you have answered before. Answer him.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a5-table.text: The past for everyone, on the verbs you know: hacer, hizo (he or she made); pescar, pescó; comprar, compró; ir, fue (he went). Nosotros: fuimos (we went). Ellos and ustedes: comieron (they ate), fueron (they went, you all went). The -ó of él and ella is stressed: compró, not compro (I buy). What you have to do: tengo que and an infinitive, tengo que ir al río. The book keeps them.
strings.lesson.ayer-en-el-pueblo.a5-recap.text: You can now say what someone else did, what you and someone did, and what they did, and what you have to do. Next time, {npc:baker}, {npc:smith} and {npc:fisher} talk about tomorrow.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.title: Mañana en el pueblo: tomorrow in the village
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.text: Session 9: what you and the village will do tomorrow, with {npc:baker}, {npc:smith} and {npc:fisher}: the future in one word (compraré, buscaré, iré; hará, trabajará), the second way to say tomorrow after voy a, and when each is used.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.summary: You can say what you will do in one word (mañana compraré pan, iré al río), promise something (buscaré madera para Luz) and say what someone else will do (Luz hará pan), and you know when voy a and the one-word future are used.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.objective: Session 9: go to the bakery and talk to {npc:baker} the baker to start the lesson “Mañana en el pueblo”
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m0-review.tex: {npc:baker} greets you and asks something you have answered before. Answer her.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m0-intro.text: Session 9: tomorrow in the village. You know one future, voy a and an infinitive: voy a comprar pan. Spanish has a second one in a single word: the whole infinitive and an ending, compraré (I will buy), comprarás (you will buy), comprará (he or she will buy), compraremos (we), comprarán (they, ustedes). The ending is stressed. Ir is iré; a few verbs change their stem: hacer is haré, hará; tener is tendré. Enter goes on, H helps, K skips a step.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m1-buy.text: She asks what you will do tomorrow (harás, you will do). Answer with comprar and the ending -é: “Mañana compraré pan”.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m1-buy.help: Say: Mañana compraré pan. It means tomorrow I will buy bread.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m1-buy.retry: Not quite. Say: Mañana compraré pan.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m1-buy.tenseR: It is about tomorrow: say the future in one word, “compraré”, not “compré” or “compro”.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m1-buy.future: That is right too. Here we practise “compraré”: Mañana compraré pan.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m1-bread.text: Tener changes its stem in the future: tendré, I will have. Listen to {npc:baker}.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m1-bread.tran: Great! Tomorrow I will have fresh bread.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m1-two.text: Two ways to say tomorrow, and both are right. Voy a and an infinitive says a plan you already have: Voy a comprar pan. The one-word future says a promise or a prediction: Mañana compraré pan. This lesson practises the second.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m2-walk.text: Press Esc, follow the arrow to {npc:smith} by the smithy and press {key:talk} to talk to him.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m2-walk.help: The smithy is the house right of the tower, with the forge by its door.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m2-walk.hud: Talk to {npc:smith} the smith at the smithy
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m2-wood.text: Luz needs wood for her oven. Promise to look for some, with buscar and -é, and say who it is for with para: “Buscaré madera para Luz”.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m2-wood.trans: Hello! Luz needs wood for the oven. What will you do?
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m2-wood.help: Say: Buscaré madera para Luz. It means I will look for wood for Luz.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m2-wood.retry: Not quite. Say: Buscaré madera para Luz.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m2-wood.tense: It is a promise: say the future in one word, “buscaré”, not “busco”.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m2-wood.futur: That is right too. Here we practise “buscaré”: Buscaré madera para Luz.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m2-go.text: Mar will fish at the river (pescará, he will fish). Ir keeps its infinitive in the future: iré, I will go. Say where you will go: “Iré al río”.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m2-go.transla: Very good! Mar will fish in the river all afternoon. Where will you go now?
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m2-go.help: Say: Iré al río. It means I will go to the river.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m2-go.retry: Not quite. Say: Iré al río.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m2-go.personR: Say it about yourself: “iré”, I will go.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m2-go.tenseRe: Say the future in one word: “iré”, not “voy” or “fui”.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m2-go.futureN: That is right too. Here we practise “iré”: Iré al río.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m3-walk.text: So go: press Esc, follow the arrow to the river (río) by the bridge, where {npc:fisher} fishes, and press {key:talk} to talk to him.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m3-walk.help: The river runs under the bridge, west of the village; {npc:fisher} stands on its bank.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m3-walk.hud: Go to {npc:fisher} at the river (río) by the bridge
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m3-day.transl: Hello! Tomorrow Luz will make bread. Domingo will work at the smithy. And I will fish in the river.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m3-day.help: “Hará” is she will make, “trabajará” he will work and “pescaré” I will fish: the future in one word, its ending stressed.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m3-day.retry: Not quite. Listen again: hará pan, trabajará, pescaré.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m3-day.option: Luz will make bread, Mar will fish.
Luz will buy bread, Mar will sell fish.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m3-luz.text: He asks what Luz will do tomorrow. Tell him what he said, about her: hacer is hará for él and ella: “Luz hará pan”.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m3-luz.help: Say: Luz hará pan. It means Luz will make bread.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m3-luz.retry: Not quite. Say: Luz hará pan.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m3-luz.person: Say it about her: “hará”, not “haré” or “harás”.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m3-luz.tenseR: It is tomorrow: say the future in one word, “hará”, not “hace” or “hizo”.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m3-luz.future: That is right too. Here we practise “hará”: Luz hará pan.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m4-review.tex: {npc:fisher} asks something you have answered before. Answer him.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m4-table.text: The future in one word, on the verbs you know: comprar, compraré (I), comprarás (you), comprará (he or she); ir, iré; buscar, buscaré; hacer, hará; tener, tendré; trabajar, trabajará; pescar, pescará. The ending is stressed. Later days: pasado mañana (the day after tomorrow), la semana que viene or la próxima semana (next week), el próximo día (the next day). A plan you have: voy a comprar pan; a promise or a prediction: mañana compraré pan. The book keeps them.
strings.lesson.manana-en-el-pueblo.m4-recap.text: You can now say what you will do, promise something and say what someone else will do, in one word, and you know when voy a says it instead. Next time, the village holds its market.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.title: El mercado: the market
strings.lesson.el-mercado.text: Session 10: market day in the village, with {npc:baker}, {npc:farmer} and the shopkeeper: the numbers from 11 to 20, the price of everything, comparing prices, poder, and selling; the market told in the past, the present and the future.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.summary: You can count to twenty, ask what everything costs (¿Cuánto es todo?), say a price is high (es muy caro) and compare two (más barata que), ask if you can pay with something (¿Puedo pagar con fruta?) and sell (vendo madera), and tell the market in three times: compré, quiero vender, venderé.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.objective: Session 10: go to the bakery and talk to {npc:baker} the baker to start the lesson “El mercado”
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k0-review.text: {npc:baker} greets you and asks something you have answered before. Answer her.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k0-intro.text: Session 10: market day, the last lesson of the village. Count to twenty, sell wood to {npc:baker}, buy apples from {npc:farmer} and compare prices, and tell the market in the three times: now, the past and tomorrow.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k1-fifteen.text: She counts her loaves for the market. Which numbers?
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k1-fifteen.help: Once, doce, trece, catorce, quince: eleven to fifteen. They end in -ce, as doce does.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k1-fifteen.retry: Not quite. Listen again: once, doce, trece.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k1-twenty.text: She counts on. Which numbers now?
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k1-twenty.help: Dieciséis is diez y seis, ten and six: dieciséis, diecisiete, dieciocho, diecinueve, and then veinte, twenty.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k1-twenty.retry: Not quite. Listen again: dieciséis, diecisiete.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k1-loaves.text: There is a market today (hoy hay mercado). She asks how many loaves she has: she counted to twenty. Tell her, with tienes (you have): “Tienes veinte panes”.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k1-loaves.translation: There is a market today! How many loaves do I have?
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k1-loaves.help: Say: Tienes veinte panes. It means you have twenty loaves.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k1-loaves.retry: Not quite. Say: Tienes veinte panes.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k1-loaves.personRetry: Say it about her: “tienes” (you have), not “tengo”.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k1-loaves.tenseRetry: She has them now: use the present, “tienes”.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k2-sell.text: Her oven needs wood (madera). Say what you want to do, with quiero and the infinitive vender (to sell): “Quiero vender madera”.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k2-sell.translation: I need wood for the oven. What do you want to do?
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k2-sell.help: Say: Quiero vender madera. It means I want to sell wood.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k2-sell.retry: Not quite. Say: Quiero vender madera.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k2-sell.personRetry: Say it about yourself: “quiero”, I want.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k2-sell.tenseRetry: It is what you want now: use the present, “quiero vender”.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k2-pay.text: She tells you her price. Pagar is to pay, and cada is each.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k2-pay.translation: I will pay you one coin for each block of wood.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k3-wood.text: Get wood to sell: press Esc, follow the arrow to the trees, aim the dot at a trunk and hold the left mouse button; with the axe (hacha) in your hand it is quick. Collect three or more: {npc:farmer}'s apples cost a coin each.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k3-wood.help: The trees stand round the village's clearing; the arrow shows the nearest one. Hold the axe to collect wood faster.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k3-back.text: Take the wood to {npc:baker} at the bakery and press {key:talk} to talk to her.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k3-back.help: The bakery is the timber house with the oven, left of the tower.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k3-back.hud: Take the wood to {npc:baker} at the bakery
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k3-sell.text: Sell her your wood, with vendo (I sell, from vender): “Vendo madera”. She pays a coin for each block.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k3-sell.help: Say: Vendo madera. It means I am selling wood.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k4-walk.text: Now buy apples with your coins: press Esc, follow the arrow to {npc:farmer} at the wheat field and press {key:talk} to talk to him.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k4-walk.help: The field is east of the square, between two houses.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k4-walk.hud: Talk to {npc:farmer} the farmer at the field
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k4-all.text: He has fifteen apples (quince manzanas) for the market. Ask the price of all of them: “¿Cuánto es todo?” Todo is everything.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k4-all.translation: Hello! There is a market today. I have fifteen apples.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k4-all.help: Say: ¿Cuánto es todo? It means how much is it all?
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k4-dear.text: Fifteen coins, more than you have! He asks if that is expensive (caro) or cheap (barato). Say it is very expensive: “Es muy caro”.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k4-dear.help: Say: Es muy caro. It means it is very expensive.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k4-dear.retry: Not quite. Say: Es muy caro.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k4-dear.personRetry: Say it about the price: “es”, it is.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k5-cheaper.text: He compares his apples with Luz's bread: an apple costs one coin, a loaf two. Say which is cheaper, with más … que: “La manzana es más barata que el pan”. Barata agrees with la manzana.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k5-cheaper.translation: An apple costs one coin, and a loaf two. Which is cheaper?
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k5-cheaper.help: Say: La manzana es más barata que el pan. It means the apple is cheaper than the bread.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k5-cheaper.retry: Not quite. Say: La manzana es más barata que el pan.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k5-cheaper.personRetry: Say it about the apple: “es”, it is.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k5-fruit.text: Can you pay with fruit instead of coins? Ask him, with puedo (I can, from poder) and pagar (to pay): “¿Puedo pagar con fruta?”
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k5-fruit.help: Say: ¿Puedo pagar con fruta? It means can I pay with fruit?
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k5-fruit.retry: Not quite. Say: ¿Puedo pagar con fruta?
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k5-tomorrow.text: He takes no fruit as money, but he buys fruit. He asks what you will sell tomorrow. Promise, with vender and the ending -é: “Mañana venderé fruta”.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k5-tomorrow.translatio: And what will you sell tomorrow?
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k5-tomorrow.help: Say: Mañana venderé fruta. It means tomorrow I will sell fruit.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k5-tomorrow.retry: Not quite. Say: Mañana venderé fruta.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k5-tomorrow.tenseRetry: It is tomorrow: say the future in one word, “venderé”, not “vendo” or “vendí”.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k5-tomorrow.futureNote: That is right too. Here we practise “venderé”: Mañana venderé fruta.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k6-buy.text: Now buy three apples with your coins: say “Quiero tres manzanas”. Three apples cost three coins; if you have fewer, sell {npc:baker} more wood first.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k6-buy.help: Say: Quiero tres manzanas. An apple costs one coin.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k7-walk.text: Press Esc, follow the arrow to the stall and press {key:talk} to talk to the shopkeeper.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k7-walk.help: The stall is on the west side of the square, by the road to the bridge.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k7-walk.hud: Talk to the shopkeeper at the stall
