strings.lesson.el-mercado.k7-bought.text: He asks what you bought at the market (compraste, you bought). Tell him, in the past: “Compré tres manzanas”.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k7-bought.translation: Hello! What did you buy at the market?
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k7-bought.help: Say: Compré tres manzanas. It means I bought three apples.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k7-bought.retry: Not quite. Say: Compré tres manzanas.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k7-bought.personRetry: Say it about yourself: “compré”, I bought.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k7-bought.tenseRetry: You bought them already: use the past, “compré”, not “compro”.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k8-review.text: He asks something you have answered before. Answer him.
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k8-table.text: At the market: ¿cuánto cuesta? for one thing, ¿cuánto es todo? for everything; caro (expensive), barato (cheap); más barata que (cheaper than), the adjective agreeing with the first thing compared. Poder: puedo and an infinitive. Vender in three times: compré tres manzanas (the past), quiero vender madera and vendo madera (now), mañana venderé fruta or voy a vender fruta (the future).
strings.lesson.el-mercado.k8-recap.text: You can now count to twenty, ask what everything costs, compare prices, ask how to pay and sell, and tell the market in the past, the present and the future. That was the last lesson of the village: every lesson is done. Practise any of them in your book, and sell wood or fruit for coins whenever you like.
strings.lesson.first-class.title: Luna's first class: please, thanks and I want
strings.lesson.first-class.text: A short class with {npc:guide}: yes, please and thank you, then the verbs I want, I have and I need.
strings.lesson.first-class.summary: You can accept politely, say thanks, and say what you want, have and need.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.title: En la panadería: at the bakery
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.text: Session 11, an optional class: bread with {npc:baker}. She shows you at the oven, in short commands (pon, echa, mezcla, saca), how to make bread; you only need to understand them. You say what you are going to do (voy a hacer pan) and what you did (hice pan), ask for flour (quiero harina) and sell a loaf (vendo pan).
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.summary: You understand Luz's commands at the oven (pon, echa, mezcla, saca), you can say what you are going to make (voy a hacer pan) and what you made (hice pan), ask for flour at the stall (quiero harina) and sell bread (vendo pan).
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.objective: Session 11: talk to {npc:baker} at the bakery to start the optional class “En la panadería”
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k0-review.text: {npc:baker} asks something you have answered before. Answer her.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k0-intro.text: {npc:baker} will show you how to make bread. Her instructions are short commands: pon (put), echa (pour), mezcla (mix), saca (take out). You only need to understand them. You do not have to take this class to bake: the oven is always open.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k1-plan.text: She plans the day. Hoy vamos a hacer pan: vamos a is “we are going to”, and she asks for your help (¿me ayudas?).
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k1-plan.translati: Today we are going to make bread. Will you help me?
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k1-answer.text: She asks what you are going to do today. Say it with voy a and the infinitive hacer (to make): “Voy a hacer pan”.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k1-answer.transla: What are you going to do today?
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k1-answer.help: Say: Voy a hacer pan. It means I am going to make bread.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k1-answer.retry: Not quite. Say: Voy a hacer pan.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k1-answer.personR: Say it about yourself: “voy a”, I am going to.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k1-answer.tenseRe: It is what you will do today: use voy a and the infinitive, “voy a hacer”.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k1-answer.present: That is right too. Here we practise “voy a hacer”: Voy a hacer pan.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k2-mezcla.text: These are her commands at the oven. Listen to the first one. What must you do?
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k2-mezcla.help: Mezcla is the command of mezclar, to mix; la cuchara is the spoon.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k2-mezcla.retry: Not quite. Listen again: mezcla con la cuchara.
Put the flour in the bowl.
Take the bread out of the oven.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k2-saca.text: One more command. What must you do?
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k2-saca.translati: Take the bread out of the oven.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k2-saca.help: Saca is the command of sacar, to take out; del horno is out of the oven.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k2-saca.retry: Not quite. Listen again: saca el pan del horno.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k2-saca.option.1: Take the bread out of the oven.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k2-saca.option.2: Put the dough in the oven.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k3-oven.text: Make bread at the oven: follow the arrow to the oven by the bakery, press {key:talk} and do what she says. Hold a thing with the number keys, choose where it goes with Tab, then press Enter. If something is missing, ask her: “Quiero madera”, “Quiero agua”.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k3-oven.help: The oven is the stone vault against the bakery's east wall. Press {key:talk} next to it. H shows the help, R repeats her command.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k3-back.text: Take your bread to {npc:baker} at the bakery and press {key:talk} to talk to her.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k3-back.help: She stands by the bakery door, left of the tower.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k4-report.text: She asks what you did (hiciste, you did). Tell her, in the past: “Hice pan”.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k4-report.help: Say: Hice pan. It means I made bread.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k4-report.personR: Say it about yourself: “hice”, I did.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k4-report.tenseRe: You made it already: use the past, “hice”, not “hago” or “voy a hacer”.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k5-walk.text: Press Esc, follow the arrow to the stall and press {key:talk} to talk to the shopkeeper. Flour costs a coin there, and he buys your bread for a coin.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k5-walk.help: The stall is on the west side of the square, by the road to the bridge.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k5-walk.hud: Talk to the shopkeeper at the stall
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k5-flour.text: He asks what you need. Flour (harina) is for your next bread: “Quiero harina”. It costs a coin.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k5-flour.help: Say: Quiero harina. It means I want flour.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k5-sell.text: Now sell him a loaf. He asks what you need again; say what you are doing: “Vendo pan” (I am selling bread). He pays a coin for each loaf.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k5-sell.help: Say: Vendo pan. It means I am selling bread. You need bread in your bag; a bake gives you two or three.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k6-review.text: He asks something you have answered before. Answer him.
strings.lesson.en-la-panaderia.k7-recap.text: You can now follow a recipe by its commands (pon, echa, mezcla, saca), say what you are going to make and what you made, ask for flour and sell bread. Bake whenever you like: bread feeds you, and a loaf sells for a coin.
